user.title: Device Routines
user.description: Device Routines adds start and stop times, run timers and a plain language schedule summary to your device pages. There is nothing to configure. If automations already switch some devices at set times, the next screen offers to give them routine controls.

abort.already_configured: Device Routines is already set up. Only one instance is supported.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Device Routines is already set up. Only one instance is supported.

skip_next.name: Skip next
skip_next.description: Skips the next action of each targeted routine: a start skips the whole run up to its stop, while a stop or a running timer is skipped alone. Calling it again extends the skip to the following action. Targets without a routine are ignored and listed in the response.

pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Pauses each targeted routine until a time or for a duration: no scheduled action runs and no timer fires until then. Manual changes still work. Targets without a routine are ignored and listed in the response.

until.name: Until
until.description: When the pause ends. Give either this or a duration.

for.name: For
for.description: How long the pause lasts. Give either this or an end time.

resume.name: Resume
resume.description: Ends the pause or skip of each targeted routine now. With Catch up on, the device is set to what its schedule expects at once. Targets without a routine are ignored and listed in the response.

enable.name: Enable
enable.description: Turns each targeted routine on, like its Routine switch. Targets without a routine are ignored and listed in the response.

disable.name: Disable
disable.description: Turns each targeted routine off until it is enabled again, like its Routine switch: nothing runs meanwhile. Targets without a routine are ignored and listed in the response.

maintenance.name: Run maintenance
maintenance.description: Runs one Device Routines maintenance action. Every action is safe to run at any time. The response lists what changed, or with a dry run, what would change.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only report what would change, without changing anything.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Defaults apply to routines created from now on; changing one never rewrites an existing routine. Saving reloads Device Routines and rebuilds every Schedule sensor.

data.default_catch_up: Catch up after a restart, for new routines
data.default_respect_manual: Respect manual changes, for new routines
data.default_late_start_window_min: Late start window, for new routines
data.assign_area: Put routines in the device's area

data_description.schedule_scope: Which devices get a Schedule sensor: every device an automation acts on, only devices with a routine, or none.
data_description.time_format: How times read in every sentence. Automatic follows the country set in Home Assistant.
data_description.default_catch_up: The starting value of Catch up for routines created from now on: after a restart, the device is put in the state its schedule expects.
data_description.default_respect_manual: The starting value of Respect manual changes for routines created from now on: a device someone switched by hand stays as it is until its next scheduled time.
data_description.default_late_start_window_min: How long after a missed start time a new routine may still start its device, for example after a restart. 0 turns late starts off.
data_description.cleanup_after_days: How long a routine automation and its helpers stay after their device is opted out or removed from Home Assistant. 0 keeps them.
data_description.assign_area: Give each routine automation the area of its device, so it shows on the area page.
data_description.on_removal: What removing Device Routines does to the routine automations. Keep turns each into a normal automation that keeps running; delete removes them with their timers and schedules.
data_description.ai_calls_per_hour: The most summaries the AI summary entity writes in one hour.
data_description.offer_conversions: Offer, in Repairs, to turn a hand written automation that does exactly what a routine does into a routine.
data_description.raise_conflict_repairs: Raise a Repairs issue when a routine and another automation switch a device in opposite directions at the same minute.
data_description.ai_task_entity: Optional; AI summaries stay off while this is empty. When you choose an AI Task entity, Device Routines sends it, through its generate data action, only the automations whose schedule it cannot read itself: one automation at a time, at most as many an hour as AI calls per hour allows, and never in the first five minutes after a start. For each it sends the trigger, condition and action blocks as written, templates included, with entities named by entity id. Aliases and descriptions are left out, devices, areas, floors and labels become numbered placeholders, and no names, states or attributes are sent. It goes to this entity only; where the entity sends it next depends on its integration (a local model keeps it in your home, a cloud service does not). Answers are kept until the automation changes and show with (AI).

devices.title: Devices with routines
devices.description: Each chosen device gets routine controls on its device page and the Routines label. A device taken off the list keeps its settings and its routine turns off; it is deleted after the clean up period.

data_description.devices: Only devices with an entity a routine can switch are listed.

suggestions.title: Suggested devices
suggestions.description: Automations switch these devices at set times. Tick the ones that should get routine controls on their device page, or leave them all unticked to skip. This list stays available in the Device Routines options.

data_description.devices: Nothing is ticked: leave it that way to skip.

error.not_eligible: {device} has no entity a routine can switch any more. Choose again.

abort.no_suggestions: No device without routine controls is switched by an automation at set times right now.

adapter_incompatible.title: Device Routines cannot read automations on this Home Assistant version
adapter_incompatible.description: Home Assistant {ha_version} does not offer what Device Routines needs for: {capabilities}. Schedule sensors stay as they were and routines keep running. Update Device Routines; the issue clears by itself once a compatible version loads.

blueprint_modified.title: The Device Routines blueprint was changed

confirm.title: Reinstall the shipped blueprint
confirm.description: The installed blueprint file differs from the one Device Routines ships, so it was left alone and routines keep running on the changed file. Submit to put the shipped blueprint back and reload the automations that use it. The changes made to the file are lost.

abort.not_loaded: Device Routines is not loaded. Enable it in Settings, Devices and services, then try again.
abort.not_fixed: The shipped blueprint could not be installed. The Home Assistant log names the reason.

invalid_inputs.title: The routine of {device} cannot run as edited

confirm.title: Restore the last valid settings
confirm.description: An edit of {automation} left inputs a routine cannot use ({reason}). The routine of {device} was turned off and nothing was overwritten. Submit to write the last valid settings back and turn the routine on again, or close this and correct the automation in its form.

abort.not_loaded: Device Routines is not loaded. Enable it in Settings, Devices and services, then try again.
abort.unknown_routine: {automation} is not a routine Device Routines manages any more, so there is nothing to do here.
abort.no_valid_settings: There are no earlier valid settings for the routine of {device} to restore. Correct {automation} in its form instead.
abort.not_fixed: The last valid settings of {device} could not be written. The Home Assistant log names the reason; try again later.

detached_routine.title: The routine of {device} is now a normal automation

confirm.title: Create a new routine
confirm.description: {automation} no longer uses the Device Routines blueprint, so the device page controls of {device} are unavailable and the integration never touches it again. Submit to create a new routine for {device} with the settings it had. {automation} stays exactly as it is: turn it off or delete it yourself if the new routine replaces it.

abort.not_loaded: Device Routines is not loaded. Enable it in Settings, Devices and services, then try again.
abort.unknown_routine: {automation} is not a routine Device Routines manages any more, so there is nothing to do here.
abort.not_fixed: The new routine of {device} could not be created. The Home Assistant log names the reason; try again later.

schedule_blocks_needed.title: The weekly schedule of {device} is empty
schedule_blocks_needed.description: The schedule helper {schedule} had to be recreated and has no blocks yet, so the routine of {device} does nothing. Open it under Settings, Devices and services, Helpers and add the blocks again. This issue clears by itself once the schedule has blocks.

write_conflict.title: A change to the routine of {device} was not saved

confirm.title: Save the change again
confirm.description: {automation} was changed by something else twice while Device Routines saved it, so the change to the routine of {device} was not written. Submit to write it again now.

abort.not_loaded: Device Routines is not loaded. Enable it in Settings, Devices and services, then try again.
abort.unknown_routine: {automation} is not a routine Device Routines manages any more, so there is nothing to do here.
abort.not_fixed: {automation} changed again while Device Routines saved it. Try again in a moment.

automation_load_failed.title: The routine of {device} does not load

confirm.title: Regenerate the automation
confirm.description: {automation} did not load, even after Device Routines regenerated it once, so the routine of {device} is off. Submit to regenerate it from the last valid settings.

abort.not_loaded: Device Routines is not loaded. Enable it in Settings, Devices and services, then try again.
abort.unknown_routine: {automation} is not a routine Device Routines manages any more, so there is nothing to do here.
abort.not_fixed: {automation} still does not load. The Home Assistant log names the reason; correct it, then try again.

conflict.title: Two automations drive {device} in opposite directions
conflict.description: {first} and {second} change {device} in opposite directions at {time}. Change one of them; this issue clears when they no longer collide.

refused_action.message: Device Routines never schedules {action}, because it would weaken safety or security.

on_time_not_supported.message: A routine cannot turn on, open or start this {domain} device, so it has no start time. Clear the start time.

same_on_and_off_time.message: The start and stop times are the same. Choose two different times.

schedule_entity_missing.message: Days is set to Weekly schedule, but no schedule is linked to the routine.

times_with_weekly_schedule.message: A routine that follows a weekly schedule takes its times from the schedule. Clear the start and stop times, or choose other days.

schedule_helper_failed.message: The weekly schedule {schedule} could not be created, so the days stay as they were. Check the Home Assistant log and try again.

duration_not_supported.message: A routine for this {domain} device does not offer this run timer.

both_durations.message: Turn off after and Turn back on after cannot both be set on one routine. Set one of them to 0.

pulse_not_supported.message: A routine for this {domain} device cannot pulse: it needs both an on and an off action.

invalid_inputs.message: The routine's automation holds settings Device Routines cannot read. Fix them in the automation editor, or change any routine setting on the device page to write them again.

store_version_unsupported.message: The Device Routines storage file has version {version}, newer than this version of Device Routines reads ({supported}). Update Device Routines, or restore a backup taken before the downgrade.

invalid_value.message: {setting} has a value a routine cannot use.

invalid_target.message: {entity} is not an entity the routine of this device can control.

unknown_device.message: Device {device} is not known to Home Assistant, or belongs to Device Routines itself.

not_eligible.message: {device} has no entity a routine can control.

not_opted_in.message: {device} has no routine controls. Add the Routines label to it, or choose it in the Device Routines options.

detached.message: The routine of {device} is a normal automation now. Create a new routine to use the controls again.

editing_unavailable.message: Routine settings cannot be changed on this Home Assistant version. The routines keep running; see the Device Routines Repairs issue.

no_routine.message: {device} has no routine yet. Set a start or stop time first.

nothing_to_skip.message: Nothing is scheduled for {device}, so there is nothing to skip.

pause_until_or_for.message: Give the pause either an end time or a duration, exactly one of them.

paused_until_in_past.message: Paused until must be in the future.

no_routine_targets.message: None of the chosen targets has a routine.

not_loaded.message: Device Routines is not loaded. Wait until it has started; if it does not start, check its entry in Devices and services and the Home Assistant log.

no_valid_settings.message: There are no earlier valid settings for the routine of {device} to restore.

unknown_routine.message: {automation} is not a routine Device Routines manages.

target_all_reserved.message: A target of all is reserved for a later version. Choose devices, entities, areas, floors or labels.

invalid_ai_task_entity.message: {setting} must be an AI Task entity, or empty.

action_skipped.name: Routine action skipped
action_skipped.description: Triggers when a routine skips a scheduled action or a countdown because it is paused or skipping.

paused.name: Routine paused
paused.description: Triggers when one or more routines are paused or skip their next action.

resumed.name: Routine resumed
resumed.description: Triggers when one or more routines run again after a pause or a skip ends.

is_paused.name: Routine is paused
is_paused.description: Tests if one or more routines are paused or skipping.

is_active.name: Routine is active
is_active.description: Tests if one or more routines are on and not paused.
